newsitem.title: USA: Property losses from Hurricane Fran seen $625 mln.
newsitem.headline: Property losses from Hurricane Fran seen $625 mln.

text.p: The insurance industry will pay about $625 million in claims to people whose property was damaged by Hurricane Fran, according to the Insurance Information Institute (III).

"The storm will not have a major impact on the financial strength of the insurance industry," said Sean Mooney, senior vice president and economist for the trade group in a statement. He said the industry had the resources to pay the claims.

Mooney said that claims are likely to involve damaged roofs, automobiles, downed trees and extensive flooding. However, while standard business and homeowners policies will cover wind damage from the storm, they do cover damage from flooding.
Flood damage is covered under policies written by the National Flood Insurance Program.

According to Boston-based Applied Insurance Research Inc, which prepared the preliminary estimate, over 80 percent of the estimated damage occurred in North Carolina, with parts of South Carolina, Virginia and Maryland also affected.

According to Mooney, Hurricane Andrew was the costliest catastrophe on record with $15.5 billion in insured property damage. Hurricane Hugo, which struck the Carolinas in 1989, cost $4.2 billion in insured losses.
